title: terraform: private deployment - refactor GPU node pools, IAM roles, networking, and state layout
author: Ethan Kim
release_notes: Refactor private Terraform modules for GPU node pools, IAM roles, networking, and backend state layout to improve upgrade/rollback safety and cross-account drift resilience. No user-facing API changes.
description:
Summary: This PR refactors the Terraform layout used for private deployments (VPC/on-prem installer path) focusing on four areas: GPU node pools, IAM roles, networking modules, and state backend layout. The primary goals are (1) make node pool semantics deterministic across upgrades, (2) reduce blast radius when rolling back or switching org accounts, (3) centralize IAM role generation to reduce duplication, and (4) migrate to a more stable remote state layout that supports partial imports for existing customers. Motivation: We observed several upgrade incidents where node pool naming drifted between modules (leading to ephemeral node replacements) and where state layout changes forced full-state imports for customers during private upgrades. This caused unexpected downtime for a small subset of Dedicated/Private customers. This change mitigates those risks and paves the way for safer zero-downtime upgrades and rollbacks.

What I changed (high-level commits summary):
- feat(terraform): introduce unified gpu_node_pool module with explicit lifecycle rules and stable naming (commit: a3d9f2c)
- refactor(terraform): move IAM role templates into modules/iam/core to dedupe policy attachments and add cross-account assume-role variables (commit: b1f4e8a)
- chore(terraform): networking: extract subnets/security-groups into modules/networking/private to support shared VPCs (commit: c5b7d11)
- docs: upgrade notes and migration guide for state layout and import steps (commit: d2e7f4a)
- test(terraform): add integration terraform plan/unit checks and CI matrix for GKE/AKS/EKS node pool shapes (commit: e9c1a3b)

Files touched (representative): modules/gpu_node_pool/main.tf; modules/gpu_node_pool/variables.tf; modules/iam/core/main.tf; modules/iam/core/outputs.tf; modules/networking/private/main.tf; modules/networking/private/outputs.tf; environments/private/backend.tf; examples/private/migration/README.md; scripts/tfstate-partial-import.sh; ci/terraform/plan-integration.yml

Key implementation notes:
- Stable naming: node pools now derive names from a hashed prefix of (deployment_id + role + major_version) and accept an override name. We added lifecycle "prevent_destroy" for user-managed volumes and optional "create_before_destroy" toggles controlled by a feature flag var.enable_create_before_destroy to support controlled rollouts.
- IAM: policies are consolidated to a single iam/core module. Where previously policies were scattered across environment overlays, the core module exposes fine-grained role templates and allows providing external role ARNs for cross-account setups.
- Networking: subnet and security-group resources are decoupled to support both per-tenant VPCs and shared VPC scenarios. The module exposes import-friendly resource IDs and clear tags to help the partial import tooling.
- State layout: backend.tf changes move from a fully-encompassing state per-environment to a split state: infrastructure state vs. components (node pools, iam, networking). We provide a migration script (scripts/tfstate-partial-import.sh) and a documented step-by-step guide in examples/private/migration/README.md. The migration strategy minimizes downtime by importing only the resource groups that change and leaving persistent infra untouched.

Testing and CI:
- CI matrix runs plan-only across supported clouds (GCP/GKE, AWS/EKS, Azure/AKS) with multiple node shapes. All pipeline checks are green after iterating on linting and provider version pinning.
- Added unit-style checks: terraform validate, tflint, checkov scan for IAM policies, and a smoke plan that ensures no accidental destroy operations on default stacks.
- Manual canary: validated migration on an internal mirror org using the migration script and performed two upgrade+rollback cycles with zero-app downtime on the canary cluster.

Review notes / conversation (excerpt):
- Sofia Patel (reviewer): "Can we get stronger guardrails on create_before_destroy? We should default to false and require an explicit opt-in from SRE for any production rollouts." — Addressed: default is false and added var.sre_approval_required boolean that gates pipeline promotion.
- Lucia Morales (reviewer): "IAM changes look good but ensure policies are audited for least privilege." — Addressed: split large policies into smaller, attachable statements and added checkov exceptions for legacy managed policies with a follow-up task.
- Aaron Chen (reviewer): "State migration is sensitive; include a dry-run mode in the script." — Addressed: scripts/tfstate-partial-import.sh now supports --dry-run and outputs exact import commands.
- Author reply: "Thanks all — responded inline and pushed three small follow-up commits to tighten defaults and add dry-run/more logging."
- Approval timeline: Sofia approved on 2025-11-16, Lucia requested one minor doc change (done), Aaron approved 2025-11-17.

CI status and merge: All CI checks passed on final run (plan, validate, lint, checkov). The PR was squashed and merged into main on 2025-11-18. Merge method: squash. Post-merge actions: created a follow-up internal ticket (ENG-8345) to schedule a phased customer migration and added a private-engineering runbook for migrations.

Rollout / rollback plan: Rollouts should be executed per the migration README. The default path is:
1) Run terraform plan in dry-run mode for your environment.
2) Run scripts/tfstate-partial-import.sh --dry-run and confirm commands.
3) Execute imports for networking and IAM first, verify stability, then import node pools.
4) Promote create_before_destroy only for non-prod canaries, validate, then opt-in for prod via SRE.
Rollback: Because we split state, rolling back a module applies only to that component; documented rollback steps are in the migration README. If rollback requires re-importing resources to the old state layout, the runbook lists exact tfsate mv/import commands.

Notes for operators: This PR does not change the hosted API surface. Customers on Private deployments will need to follow migration steps when upgrading to the new release. We coordinated with Solutions Engineering to prepare migration templates for early customers.
